143K likes, 2,474 comments - shivesh17 on April 15, 2025: "Still trying to wrap my head around this… but I DID IT. I BOUGHT A HOUSE.

this has been my dream for so many years now & it’s one of those v rare occasions where I’m so proud of myself🥹🥰

I’ve quite literally grown up on the internet—started sharing my life here when I was still in school, kept at it through undergrad, and eventually took the leap to become a full-time content creator. In these 10+ years, I’ve shared all my big & small milestones with YOU- you’ve been there through all the highs, lows, and everything in between♥️

As I turn 29 next week, I’m beyond grateful to have had so many of you cheer me on & encourage me to chase my dreams🥹 

I’ve just uploaded an empty house tour on my YouTube channel—click the link in my bio to watch 👀 Here’s to new beginnings, and to building a home filled with love, warmth, and memories.".

27K likes, 366 comments - shivesh17 on September 16, 2022: "5 years, 4 cookbooks 💫 my babies! 

Working on each of these books has taught me so much and I wanted to share a few things with you- 

✨Getting started is the most important part
When the offer came to me for my first book in the year 2018, I thought I wasn't prepared enough and a sense of doubt was a constant companion. Even after taking up the offer many times, I felt stuck, however, by the end, it became the biggest learning curve in my life. The entire experience was surreal and a big milestone in my baking journey. So I would say that don't be intimidated by opportunities that come your way, grab them with open arms, without any worry as every adventure requires that first big step.

✨Everyone has a role to play in this journey
When I was working on the first book I was working all alone and didn't have a team back then. However, shortly I realized that it is impossible to do everything on your own if you want to grow and have a good quality product. I also realized that more than your strengths, you need to be aware of your weaknesses and delegate them to a team that can help you achieve your goals. After the first book, I started building a team and then they say the rest is history. My last three book writing journeys have been super smooth and enjoyable hence making it a rewarding process not only for me but my team as well.

✨Feedback is very important 
As an individual working on something that takes a long time, say about a year or two to produce, it becomes easy to develop a tunnel vision without realizing that the product needs constant feedback.
I always want the final product to be valuable to my audience and therefore I feel it is important to incorporate certain feedback while working on the product. Hence I would highly recommend keeping the feedback journey a continuous one in whatever aspect of your life you are present.
For example, for all my books I made it a point to send out the recipes to a couple of friends for a fresh perspective and understand the user journey up close. This has helped me take a pause and understand the minor tweaks I need to make so that the audiences enjoy the recipes to the fullest. 

To many more 💫".

8,032 likes, 1,033 comments - shivesh17 on October 9, 2026: "Episode 4 of I Need to Try This💁🏻‍♂️, where I try the viral desserts taking over the internet 👀Today, we’re making EGGLESS CHOCOLATE CRÉMEUX 🍫🤎 Rich, silky, super creamy and everything a chocolate lover could dream of 🥹And trust me, this one is SO GOOD🤌🏻

1 cup milk
6tbsp sugar
2tbsp corn flour 
3cups cream
1/4 cup butter(55g)
600 grams Chocolate

Method-
1. Take a heavy bottomed pan and place it over medium heat.
2. ⁠Add in milk,sugar,cornflour, cream and butter.
3. ⁠Keep whisking the mixture till everything combines and comes to a boil. Let it slightly thicken.
4. ⁠Once done, pour the hot mixture over chopped chocolate and mix it well. The chocolate will melt from the heat and you will achieve a silky smooth mixture.
5. ⁠Pour it into the container and surface wrap it properly.Refrigerate overnight.
6. ⁠Once set use it to frost or fill your cakes.

Recreating: @mattadlard

Comment DISNEY to get the link to book this experience 🤍

30K likes, 1,367 comments - shivesh17 on October 2, 2026: "Episode 3 of I Need to Try This💁🏻‍♂️, where I try the viral desserts taking over the internet 👀This time, it’s Bala Biana, and look at that crunch 🤤✨ With that crispy shell and the candy surprise inside, I knew I had to try this one for myself❤️And yes, it definitely lived up to the hype🥳

Ingredients
For the Coconut Candy
1 tablespoon butter
1¼ cups desiccated coconut
1 cup condensed milk

For the Caramel Coating
1 cup sugar
½ cup water
1 teaspoon white vinegar or lemon juice

Instructions
1. Add the butter, desiccated coconut and condensed milk to a heavy-bottomed pan.
2. Cook the mixture over low to medium-low heat, stirring continuously.
3. Continue cooking until the mixture becomes thick enough to pull away from the sides and bottom of the pan. Transfer the mixture to a plate or bowl and allow it to cool until comfortable enough to handle.
4. Once the mixture has cooled, lightly grease your hands with oil and roll small portions of the mixture into balls. Place them on a parchment-lined tray or plate and allow them to cool completely.
5. To make the caramel, add the sugar, water and vinegar or lemon juice to a clean, heavy-bottomed saucepan. Place it over medium heat and allow the sugar to dissolve.
6. Let the syrup cook until it develops a clear golden-amber colour.
7. Insert a toothpick into each coconut ball and dip each ball into the hot caramel, turning it gently so that the coconut filling gets a thin, even coating.
8. Allow the excess caramel to drip off before placing the candy onto parchment paper. Allow the Bala Baiana to cool completely at room temperature before serving.

Recreating @nids.lid 💫
